record.original_question: Find a variational formulation for systems of material particles moving in R^d with d > 1 that stick on collision, for both potential and non-potential flows, and that remains flexible enough to describe shock formation and evolution in multidimensional Burgers dynamics.

evidence.quote: Problem 5. Find a variational description of the system of material particles, moving in Rd with d > 1 and sticking upon collision, for both potential and non-potential fluid flows. This formulation should be sufficiently flexible to describe the formation and development of shock waves in the system described by the multi-dimensional Burgers equation. Remark 3.3. The above variational principle should be closely related to the models of adhesion particle dynamics studied in [122]. It seems to give the same results for a finite number of sticking particles. However, the approach in [122] is fundamentally one-dimensional, while the approach described above may be extended to higher dimensions as well. 7

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a system of finitely many (or, more generally, a continuum of) material particles moving in Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $d>1$. The particles are assumed to obey the sticky-collision rule: whenever two or more particles occupy the same position at the same time, they merge into a single particle whose mass equals the sum of the masses and whose momentum equals the sum of the momenta of the colliding particles, after which the merged particle continues to move and obey the same rule. The macroscopic continuum limit of such systems is expected to describe weak (in particular shock) solutions of the multidimensional pressureless dynamics
$$\partial_t \rho + \nabla\cdot(\rho v)=0,\qquad \partial_t(\rho v)+\nabla\cdot(\rho v\otimes v)=0,$$
including the case where $v$ is the gradient of a potential (modeling the multidimensional inviscid Burgers equation $\partial_t v + (v\cdot\nabla)v = 0$) as well as the non-potential case.

Problem: Construct a variational principle (i.e., an action functional on a suitable class of admissible mass-flow / trajectory configurations, together with appropriate admissibility/entropy-type constraints) whose minimizers, critical points, or otherwise variationally selected solutions coincide with sticky-particle dynamics for arbitrary finite particle configurations in $\mathbb{R}^d$ ($d>1$), and which, in the continuum limit, describes the formation and subsequent evolution of shock waves for the multidimensional Burgers equation, in both the potential and non-potential settings. The formulation must be intrinsically multidimensional (not reducible to a one-dimensional construction along characteristics) and must remain meaningful through and beyond the first time of mass concentration.
artifact.status_search_result: A variational (Lax–Oleinik–type) principle is known in one dimension for adhesion/sticky-particle dynamics, but the multidimensional case remains unresolved: recent work shows that in $d\ge 2$ sticky-particle solutions are non-unique (infinitely many admissible weak solutions can be produced via convex integration for planar Riemann data), and no fully satisfactory intrinsically multidimensional variational selection principle covering both potential and non-potential flows has been established. The problem appears open as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: On the sticky particle solutions to the multi-dimensional pressureless Euler equations
status_evidence.snippet: For the two-dimensional pressureless Euler system with planar Riemann initial data, there exist infinitely many bounded admissible weak solutions by convex integration; sticky particle solutions form a subset of dissipative solutions.
status_evidence.claim: Non-uniqueness and lack of a canonical variational selection in d>1 indicate the problem is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Generalized variational principles ... adhesion particle dynamics (E, Rykov, Sinai)
status_evidence.snippet: Global weak solutions constructed via a Lax-Oleinik-type variational principle for adhesion particle dynamics.
status_evidence.claim: Variational principle is well-developed in the one-dimensional setting, motivating but not resolving the higher-dimensional problem.

status_evidence.title: Burgers' equation and the sticky particles model
status_evidence.snippet: Sticky particles models with velocity equal to the entropy solution of inviscid Burgers, predominantly in 1D.
